error_message: "The one-click link expired; open a new one." shown while the CloudFormation stack was still running
root_cause: Two faults. (1) The poll re-checked the token expiry client-side with Date.parse(body.expiresAt) <= Date.now(), comparing a server timestamp to the browser clock. /status only ever returns pendingToken:true for a token the DB considers unexpired, so that branch could only fire on clock skew — any browser running ahead was told the link had expired mid-deploy. (2) The TTL was 15 min measured from link generation, so it had to cover console dwell time AND the full stack build.
fix: Deleted the client-side expiry branch (server is authoritative) and dropped expiresAt from the client status type. Raised ttlMs to 60 min. Rewrote the message: an expired token makes the callback 403, the template treats non-2xx as FAILED, so the stack rolls back and deletes the IAM user by itself — telling the user to open a new link immediately would collide on the stack name.

error_message: webhooks.test.ts 'retries on failure with the 1m/5m/30m/2h/8h schedule' — AssertionError: expected null to match object { status, statusCode } at tests/integration/webhooks.test.ts:243
root_cause: NOT YET DIAGNOSED. Confirmed pre-existing: reproduces identically at commit 052dc06, before the phase-8 instance-admin work. deliver() returns null for the second delivery id (id2) after a thrown-fetch failure, where the test expects a delivered/204 result.
fix: None yet. Verified out of scope for phase 8/9 (org-level connections) — recorded so it is not mistaken for a regression from that work.

error_message: build: src/app/app/settings/RetentionForm.tsx(7,10): error TS2305: Module './actions' has no exported member 'updateRetentionAction'
root_cause: To check whether a failing test was pre-existing, ran `git checkout <old-sha> -- apps/web/src apps/web/tests` and then `git checkout HEAD -- ...` to restore. HEAD did not yet contain the in-progress task's edits, so every UNCOMMITTED change to an already-tracked file was destroyed. Newly created files survived (checkout does not delete untracked files), which made the loss partial and easy to miss — the next commit captured only the new files.
fix: Redid the lost edits. Rule: never `git checkout <sha> -- <paths>` while uncommitted work exists. Commit (or `git stash`) first, or check the baseline by reading the old file with `git show <sha>:<path>` instead of touching the working tree.

error_message: webhook-loop.test.ts: 'Invalid environment: APP_URL: APP_URL must be a full URL incl. protocol' thrown from billingConfig() via src/jobs/handlers/billing-meter.ts:54 at module scope
root_cause: The file starts a real pg-boss worker, which imports jobs/handlers/index.ts, which imports billing-meter.ts — and that calls billingConfig() -> loadEnv() at MODULE SCOPE. The test never set APP_URL (it never has, since the initial release), so it only passed when another integration file sharing the same vitest worker process had already set it. Pure isolation luck; it surfaced when file scheduling shifted.
fix: Set `process.env.APP_URL ??= "http://localhost:3000"` in its beforeAll, as every other integration file does. The deeper smell is billing-meter.ts reading env at import time rather than inside the handler — worth revisiting if it bites again.

error_message: User report: the AWS one-click connect always expires before it completes
root_cause: POST /api/setup/aws/callback burns the one-time token on its first line (consumeSetupToken) and only then runs connectWithKeys, which creates an SES configuration set, an SNS topic, a subscription and an event destination in the tenant account. That takes tens of seconds. For the whole of that window the wizard's 3s poll saw connected:false AND pendingToken:false, and the client treated exactly that pair as 'the link expired' - so a flow that had in fact succeeded was reported as expired every time.
fix: Added inFlightSetupToken(purpose, user, team, withinMs): a token consumed, not failed, and consumed within 5 minutes. /status returns it as `inFlight` and QuickCreate keeps polling (and changes its copy to 'Setting up SES in your account'). revokePendingSetupTokens now DELETEs superseded tokens instead of setting consumedAt, which would have forged the same in-flight state for a link the user abandoned. Covered by 4 new cases in tests/integration/setup-tokens.test.ts.

error_message: User report (with screenshot): the campaign preview shows the email on a dark slab - everything below the content is near-black instead of the page background
root_cause: renderBlocks put background:#f3f4f6 on <body> only. A document shorter than its viewport paints the ROOT element's background over the rest of the canvas, and <html> had none - so the area below the email fell through to the browser's default canvas. The dashboard sets color-scheme: dark, which inherits into a srcdoc iframe, making that default near-black. Not only a preview bug: Gmail and Apple Mail render in the reader's dark mode, and an unpainted root lets the client pick the background.
fix: Paint <html> as well as <body>, declare color-scheme: light on the root plus the two meta tags, and make the wrapper table full-height. Added components/ui/EmailPreview.tsx, which also wraps bare body fragments (template HTML mode) in a light document and adds a desktop/phone width toggle.

error_message: e2e: locator.click timed out waiting for getByRole('button', { name: 'Add Button', exact: true })
root_cause: The palette tile had title={`Add ${label}`} but no aria-label, so its accessible name was its own text content - 'Button', 'Image'. A screen reader reading the palette announced 'Button, button' and 'Image, button': the block is named and the verb is lost. The e2e failure was the symptom, not the bug.

error_message: e2e: page.waitForURL('**/app/templates/designed') timed out - creating a template from the visual editor silently failed
root_cause: createTemplate parsed CreateTemplateInput BEFORE compiling the design, and a design-authored draft has no bodyHtml of its own - it sent '' and hit bodyHtml.min(1). The editor would have had to invent a plausible HTML body purely to get past validation.
fix: Compile the design first and substitute the compiled body into the object that is parsed (withCompiledBody). The contract now validates the markup that is actually stored, and the caller's bodyHtml is replaced rather than overridden afterwards - closing the last way body_html and design could disagree. Note the create and update schemas differ on an empty text part: create omits, update sends null.

error_message: e2e: locator.click timed out waiting for getByRole('button', { name: 'Footer', exact: true })
root_cause: The layout row renders a name and a description inside one button, so its accessible name is both lines concatenated: 'Footer A rule, your address, and the line the law wants'. A screen reader announces that as one run-on string, naming the thing and burying the verb. Same class as bug-007 (the palette tile) - the e2e failure was the symptom, not the bug.
fix: aria-label={`Insert the ${name} layout`} on the row. Second occurrence of this pattern, so it is now a cerebrum learning rather than only a bug entry.

error_message: tests/integration/webhooks.test.ts:243 AssertionError: expected null to match object { status: 'delivered', statusCode: 204 } - red locally and in CI on master
root_cause: A time bomb, not a product bug. The test pins t0 = 2026-08-25T10:00:00Z and threads it through every deliver() call except two near the end, which fell back to the real clock. By then failingSince is t0+1s, so the disable rule (now - failingSince >= 24h) compared a fixed 2026-08-25 against today. Once the wall clock passed t0+24h the ECONNREFUSED call disabled the webhook as a side effect, and the next deliver() returned null early on !w.enabled. Green the day it was written, red every day after. It had been carried as a genuine pre-existing failure.
fix: Passed an explicit now (t0 + 1e6, then +1s) to both trailing deliver() calls so the whole test runs on one fixed clock, with a comment saying why. Audited the other fixed-date suites (billing-entitlements, billing-rollup, billing-actions): they thread their own NOW through every call and never mix in the wall clock.

error_message: CI: packages/sdk/tests/types-parity.test.ts(202-207) error TS2322: Type 'true' is not assignable to type 'false'
root_cause: The SDK ships hand-written types so its .d.ts has no dependency on zod or the private shared package, and types-parity.test.ts pins each one to the contract it mirrors with a compile-time Mutual<> tuple. Adding columns, per-block presentation and the body theme to the campaign contract flipped four entries to false. It was invisible locally because the parity half is enforced by tsc, not vitest - vitest transpiles without type-checking, so the suite runs green with a broken tuple (the file even says so).
fix: Mirrored every new field in packages/sdk/src/types.ts (align/color, button colour+textColor+corners+fullWidth, image align/width/corners, divider colour, LeafBlock/ColumnsBlock/ColumnLayout, CampaignTheme on create/update/object) and widened the guard: parity entries for LeafBlock, ColumnsBlock and CampaignTheme plus run-time enum checks against BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS, CORNER_STYLES, COLUMN_LAYOUTS, FONT_FAMILIES, IMAGE_WIDTHS and CONTENT_WIDTHS. Added a minor changeset for `sendsprite`.
